h1: M Grand Hotel Bueng Kan — a budget-friendly city hotel with spacious rooms and easy parking
intro: Bueng Kan is a small province where accommodation choices are still limited, and most people who come here drive in, stopping over before Phu Tok or the Naka Cave. M Grand Hotel is a budget-friendly city hotel that reviewers mention for its spacious, reasonably clean rooms and free parking. It's a small property of 30 rooms with free Wi-Fi, bikes to borrow and a Thai massage service. It's not a luxury stay, but it works for anyone who wants a clean bed at a light price. From approx. body.html: M Grand Hotel sits at Moo 10, Non Sombun sub-district, in Mueang Bueng Kan. It's a small property of around 30 rooms, pitched as budget accommodation for travellers — self-drivers exploring the area, business visitors passing through, and people using Bueng Kan as a base before Phu Tok and the Naka Cave. The thing reviewers agree on is that the rooms are larger than you'd expect for the money, with a quiet, restful atmosphere.

Room types run from Standard Single and Standard Double up to a Family Room for larger groups. Rooms come with air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen TV, a kettle and Wi-Fi. To be fair, this is a hotel built around price rather than newness — some reviews praise the spacious, clean rooms, while others flag dated room conditions and inconsistent housekeeping at times. If you expect a brand-new, modern fit-out, this isn't it; but if you're after a reasonably clean bed at a light price, it holds up.
"Spacious room, nice and quiet, easy parking and friendly staff — for this price in Bueng Kan it's good value."

Something self-drivers love here is the free, easy parking, which matters a lot in a province where you rely on your own vehicle. The hotel has free Wi-Fi, bikes to borrow for a ride around town, and a Thai massage service to unwind after a long drive. Breakfast isn't included in the room rate automatically, but you can add it for around 100 baht per person, or find a morning eatery in town. A common complaint is that on-site dining options are limited, so if you get hungry late you may need to rely on places outside.

Be clear about the location. M Grand is in the Bueng Kan city area, on the Non Sombun side — easy to reach by car, but not on the Mekong riverfront or in the heart of the shopping area. Some reviews note it feels a little removed from the city centre, with a drive needed to reach the river or markets. But for anyone planning to drive out to Phu Tok (about 18 km) or the Naka Cave at Bueng Khong Long, this spot works as a morning launch point. The area around the hotel is fairly quiet, good for getting a full night's rest.

Honestly, M Grand Hotel suits self-drivers exploring Bueng Kan who want a budget stay that's reasonably clean. You get a spacious room, free parking, bikes to borrow and a quiet atmosphere, at a price that's hard to find in a province with limited options. Review scores are mixed — Booking.com gives it around 6.8 from 32 reviews, praising value, staff and fast Wi-Fi, while TripAdvisor has reviews flagging room condition and cleanliness. The trade-offs to accept are that it's a budget-focused property with inconsistent rooms and upkeep, and it isn't on the river — if you can live with those three things, it's a usable, light-on-the-wallet pick in town.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask to see the room before check-in if you can, and pick one that's just been cleaned, since room quality is inconsistent. If you're travelling as a group or family, the Family Room is better value than booking several separate rooms. Borrowing the hotel's bikes for an evening ride around town is an easy thing to do. And if you're headed to Phu Tok or the Naka Cave, an early start from here buys you a full day of sightseeing.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — M Grand Hotel Bueng Kan

faq.q: Where is M Grand Hotel Bueng Kan and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 159 Moo 10, Non Sombun sub-district, Mueang Bueng Kan, in the city area. It's easy to reach by car with free parking, around a 10-minute drive from the town's shops and roughly 15 minutes from the Mekong riverfront. It works well as a base before driving out to Phu Tok (about 18 km) or the Naka Cave at Bueng Khong Long.

faq.q: How much does M Grand Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 730/night for a Standard Single. Standard Double and Twin rooms run about THB 830–880, and the Family Room for larger groups is around THB 1,250. All rooms have air-con, a fridge and a TV; prices vary by date and package, so always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is M Grand Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for self-drivers exploring Bueng Kan who want a budget stay with spacious rooms, free parking and a quiet atmosphere. It works as a base before Phu Tok and the Naka Cave, and is about value rather than design or river views.

faq.q: Are the rooms at M Grand Hotel clean, and is there anything to watch out for?
faq.a: Reviews are mixed. Some praise the spacious, clean rooms, while others flag dated room conditions and inconsistent housekeeping. It's worth asking to see the room before check-in if you can, and choosing one that's just been cleaned. Treat it as a usable budget stay rather than a premium hotel.

faq.q: Does M Grand Hotel have breakfast and a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool. Breakfast isn't included in the room rate automatically, but you can add it for around 100 baht per person, or find a morning eatery in town. The hotel has free Wi-Fi, bikes to borrow and a Thai massage service.

faq.q: Is M Grand Hotel close to Phu Tok and the Naka Cave?
faq.a: It works as a base. Phu Tok is about 18 km away (~30-min drive), while the Naka Cave at Bueng Khong Long is farther and needs a drive. Many people stay in Bueng Kan city and set off early to visit both. The hotel's free parking makes it convenient for self-drivers.
